ctx.x: No. Actually I never thought about it until Duke Ellington died. Before that, you know it was just a Japanese traditional concept, or being Japanese playing jazz was some sort of a handicap. When I was growing up in Japan as a player, they always said that Filipino people have better feeling than Japanese, and indeed the Filipino players played better than us, and it’s simply because they have a longer history. They weren’t under — they were colonized by America so they are more exposed for jazz, much longer than…

So that has been going on for a long time. When Duke Ellington died, it was ’73, or ’74 I think, and there was a Village Voice, Nat Hentoff had a memoir. And he was talking about that fact that Duke was, how proud he was about his race. And he was pointing out so many music was based on his race, which I knew some…

And I never thought I am having a difficult time. Because everybody else did I thought. When I look back I think those times were very important times.
